title: Routine Glaucoma Follow-Up

patient.name: Mr Rajasekaran s/o Pillai
patient.presenting_complaint: Routine glaucoma follow-up — on latanoprost eye drops for 6 months

history.hpc: Mr Raja is here for his 6-month glaucoma review. He says he has been using his eye drops every night but sometimes forgets. He has no eye pain. He says his vision 'seems okay' but he has not done a formal check recently. He has not had any new symptoms. He still drives for work.
history.pmhx: Primary open-angle glaucoma, both eyes, diagnosed 6 months ago. No other eye conditions.
medications: Latanoprost 0.005% eye drops — one drop each eye at night
history.social_hx: Non-smoker. Does not drink alcohol. Lives with family.

investigations.va_distance: RE: LogMAR 0.1 (6/7.5). LE: LogMAR 0.2 (6/9). Tested using LogMAR chart at 4 metres.
investigations.va_near: RE: N8 at 35cm. LE: N8 at 35cm. Tested using N chart.
investigations.iop_nct: RE: 18 mmHg. LE: 20 mmHg. Three NCT readings taken per eye, average recorded.

diagnosis: Glaucoma — stable IOP on current medication. VA adequate for driving. Findings to be reviewed by doctor.

immediate: Record VA and IOP accurately on patient records
Note that patient occasionally forgets drops — flag this to the doctor
Hand over documentation to doctor for review
follow_up: Doctor will review IOP trend and visual field
patient_education: Explain importance of using drops every night without skipping
Advise patient to inform DVLA/traffic authority if vision deteriorates
Remind patient to attend all follow-up appointments

key_points: Asks about eye drop compliance (is patient using drops correctly?)
Asks about any new visual symptoms (pain, halos, sudden vision changes)
Asks about occupation — driving is relevant for visual standards
Records current medications and confirms correct drop name and frequency
Performs distance VA using LogMAR chart at correct distance (4 metres)
Records VA correctly using LogMAR notation (e.g. 0.1, 0.2)
Performs near VA using N chart at 35cm
Performs NCT correctly: explains to patient, takes 3 readings per eye, records average
Identifies this as a routine glaucoma follow-up (not an emergency)
Recognises that VA and IOP values are within acceptable range
Flags medication non-compliance as an issue to raise with doctor
Does not make clinical decisions — refers findings to doctor appropriately
Educates patient on importance of drop compliance without being dismissive
Performs procedures in the correct sequence: history → VA → IOP → handover
